title: The Waters of El Manantial
story:
James stepped off the ancient stone bench at Las Milpas Crossroads and committed his paws to the unmapped dirt trail heading south. He had walked past the tall cobblestone archways of Oakhaven. He had walked past the pine-scented paths of Cloudveil Pass. He had walked past the ancient aqueducts of the upper terraces, and now every step carried him further into terrain that Barnaby’s parchment had never claimed. Pulling out his polished brass compass, James watched the thin needle sway and settle, pointing straight along the winding reddish earth.

The valley stretched wide and lush around him, framed by emerald rows of tall maize stalks that whispered in the mountain afternoon breeze. Wild marigolds and purple blossoms spilled over crumbling stone field walls, humming with lazy bumblebees. James paused beside a stone wall, pulling his green sea-glass from his satchel to hold it against his eye. Through the cool glass, the sunlit fields shifted into a glowing, translucent realm of jade and shadow, reminding him that even unfamiliar places carried the quiet magic of his distant canopy home.

By late afternoon, the trail descended toward a hollow where the gentle murmur of rushing water echoed through the trees. Here sat El Manantial, a sheltered roadside spring where clear groundwater trickled from a carved stone spout into a long timber trough. Moss covered the wooden edges, and smooth river pebbles glinted beneath the sparkling current. James climbed onto the lip of the trough, dipping his dusty paws into the cool water and watching the ripples disturb the sky’s reflection.

As the sun began to dip behind the high western ridges, casting long violet shadows across the valley floor, James sat quietly on the damp timber edge. A single brown leaf floated softly onto the water’s surface, swirling twice before drifting down the overflow channel toward the lower valley. James watched it go, feeling the quiet rhythm of the road settling deep into his bones as the first stars appeared above the mountain peaks.
location: El Manantial spring along the southern valley trail
